items.note: The page runs the bit network on b-digit fields, charges each edge its rank in smaller interchanges, gets F_k <= (s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), solves it, and then removes the width and row restrictions, following the paper's Section on faster interchange. It also explains why tau is barely below 1: c = m(1-eta) with eta > 20*2^{-50}.
As the assignment asks, the page only states and links it: 'a shear by an edge matrix costs as many interchanges of pairs of b-digit fields as its rank, plus O(V) further work' (on matrix-shear.md).

'Write each chunk as m consecutive b=e/m digit fields, giving vectors H,D over Z/q^bZ', the same construction as the paper. The k=0 case is handled later by 'F_0=O(1) from the single-digit operation'.
'row Wx+w-1 goes to stream w as row x' within each prefix matches the paper's r=Wg+(w-1). The page renames g to x because g is the gap.

It does not say that this commutation is why the invariant proof carries over, or that the row split supplies the common address set.

The page reads the logical input as Phi_{-M_in(w)} f_w, has the network route input w to role rho(w), and uses Phi_{M'}Phi_M=Phi_{M'+M} with M_out(rho(w))-M_in(w)=I_m to get f'_{rho(w)}=Phi_{I_m} f_w, exactly as the paper does.
Merging row x of role rho(w) back to its original row undoes rho, so Phi_{I_m}, the shear H<-H+D, holds on every row, scratch rows included, as in the paper.

items.note: 'The interchange of the two full chunks is D<-D-H, then H<-H+D, then D<-H-D' is asserted. The page does not show that the composition is the swap, though it correctly notes that only the middle shear uses the circuit and the outer updates are linear scans.

s is defined as the sum of the ranks of A_i, and each edge costs rank(A_i) interchanges on its role stream of volume V/W, so 'The number of recursive calls is the sum of the edge ranks, exactly s' follows.
'F_k <= cF_{k-1}+O(1), where c=s/W is the number of calls s times the volume fraction 1/W of each', with F_0=O(1) from the single-digit operation, matches the paper's recurrence.
The page unrolls the recurrence to a geometric sum and bounds the cases c<=1 and c>1 separately, as the paper does.
'Unrolling ... gives F_k=O(sum_{j=0}^k c^j) ... with c=s/W<m^tau.'
'If c<=1, every term is at most 1, so the sum is <= k+1=O(m^{k tau}).'
'(c^{k+1}-1)/(c-1)=O(c^k), and c^k<m^{k tau}.' This is correct.
'Hence, since e=m^k, F_k=O(e^tau).'

errors.quote: Let $F_k$ be the time per unit volume at width $m^k$.
errors.problem: Time divided by volume depends on the shape (row count, spectator lengths), so this does not define a function of k. The paper defines F_k as 'a uniform upper bound for time divided by logical volume', and that uniformity is what lets the bound apply to each recursive call.

This sum bounds only the power-width calls. The paper calls it 'the sum of the costs' of those calls and bounds the rest separately: high-part movement O(V log 2e)=O(Ve^tau), padding and unpadding, and descriptor cost O(V). The final bound still holds.
